title: Elora BIA interim board and Belwood Hall renovation
subtitle: Also: Hydro annual meeting, asset management plan, Farley Park, water grant, water tower contract, 2026 budget deferral.
overview: Council replaced the Elora Business Improvement Area board with an interim board, after the Township Solicitor advised that more members had been appointed than the 1992 establishing by-law allows. Council amended the staff plan so the Mayor, rather than a councillor, sits on the interim board {{vote:m6}}. Staff said a general meeting to elect a new board would follow in early to mid July. Several board members and a resident spoke against the change.

Council directed staff to prepare construction-ready documents for the full Belwood Hall renovation, with a Class B budget due in September and a search for extra funding. It also approved the 2025 Asset Management Plan, applied for provincial water-infrastructure funding for Carlton Place and Victoria Street in Elora, and awarded the Bridge Street water tower overcoat contract to C3 Industrial. Council signed agreements for Farley Park and the BT Corner restoration, which a donor couple is funding.

Council approved the Centre Wellington Hydro shareholder items, and received the Active Transportation and Mobility Plan for information. It deferred the 2026 budget recommendations to July 14. The mayor reported that nothing came out of the closed session held before the meeting.

decisions.detail: Council passed a by-law repealing part of By-law 2025-20 and appointing an interim Board of Management for the Elora BIA, with the Mayor replacing Councillor Jefferson {{vote:m6}}.
Council directed staff to prepare construction-ready documents for the full scope, return in September with a Class B budget, and report on funding sources.
Council approved the 2024 Shareholder Direction and the 2024 annual reports and audited financial statements for the three Hydro-related companies.
Council approved the plan, which sets out the state of Township assets, levels of service and a financing strategy.

decisions.item: Carlton Place and Victoria Street grant
decisions.detail: Staff will apply to the Municipal Housing Infrastructure Program water stream for the Elora reconstruction, with signing authority delegated to senior staff if the application succeeds.
Council awarded RFT#41-25 to C3 Industrial at an upset limit of $345,475.53 excluding HST and revised the project funding.
Council authorized the Mayor and Clerk to sign the Parkland Development Agreement with Keating Construction (2004) Limited.
Council deferred a decision on receiving the staff budget recommendations to the July 14 meeting.

debate: Delegates from the Elora BIA board argued the over-appointment was a long-standing practice that councils had repeated, not misconduct. They said the board had already asked council to update the by-law and planned to reduce its size, so an interim board was unnecessary and disruptive at the start of tourism season.

Delegates also objected to staff serving on the interim board in place of volunteers, and questioned the staff time and cost involved. A resident said the process set a troubling precedent for governance and transparency. Staff replied that current members could stand for election at the general meeting, and that the Fergus BIA would be reviewed afterwards.

On the BIA by-law, the amendment swapping the Mayor for a councillor was put forward to avoid placing a councillor on a staff-heavy interim board. A recorded vote followed, with some councillors expressing reservations or abstaining.

On Belwood Hall, councillors voiced concern about the funding gap, the longer construction timeline and keeping community groups such as the Lions in use of the space. One councillor asked that naming-rights sponsorship not displace the Belwood name. Staff said the wind turbine reserve would be largely used up.

On the 2026 budget, one councillor asked for deferral because the agenda was published only two business days earlier and the day had been long. Councillors also raised the lack of a public engagement step and a shorter amendment window under strong mayor powers; the Mayor agreed to bring it back in July.
